Subject: NovaRetail: kickoff + model context questions

Hi Priya —

Thanks again for the intro call today. Quick summary of what we need so your team can recommend model options and a sizing baseline:

- Use cases: product description generation (templated + freeform), search relevance reranking, short QA (customer-facing answers from internal KB).
- Anticipated traffic: 45 RPS peak across regions (US primary), estimated average 12 RPS, with daily burst windows (11am–1pm PST).
- Typical prompt / expected response lengths:
  • Templates: ~120 prompt tokens, ~80 response tokens
  • Freeform generation: ~400 prompt tokens (context + user notes), ~600 generated tokens
  • Reranker/QA: short prompts, responses ~60–120 tokens
- Context needs: we will frequently attach up to ~8k tokens of product metadata (structured + snippets). Occasionally (internal escalations) we will want a full 30k-character purchase history blob — not frequent.
- Compliance: must not send PII for storage; we can redact client IDs before sending. SOC2 questionnaire incoming.

Attached is a quick token profile export from our staging logs (novaretail_token_profile.csv). Can you propose a shortlist of model variants, recommended context window choices, and a rough monthly token estimate we should budget for? Also indicate whether Hosted API is fine or we should plan Dedicated for predictability.

We’re targeting a beta launch in mid-July — would like a short implementation plan and a recommended canary rollout cadence.

Thanks,
Sophie
Sophie Tran
Head of Data Products, NovaRetail

Summary from logs (attached):
- Traffic profile: average ~12 RPS (steady), peak bursts up to 45 RPS during business hours.
- Request mix (by volume): 52% rerank/QA, 30% templated generation, 18% freeform generation.
- Estimated tokens (conservative): avg tokens per request (prompt + response) = 380 tokens; projected monthly tokens = 12 RPS * 60 * 60 * 24 * 30 * 380 ≈ 1.19B tokens/month. (See CSV for hour-by-hour.)

Initial model shortlist suggestions (please comment):
1) RedGem-13B-4k (quantized) — good latency for rerank and templated gen, cheaper unit cost, 4k context.
2) Titan-40B-32k (v2) — higher quality for freeform generation and long context windows; recommend for end-user freeform and occasional 8k+ context.
3) CompactChat-7B-8k — fast, cheap option for QA and rerank when quality lower bound acceptable; use as a fallback/burst variant.

Questions for infra/product:
- Marcus: given 45 RPS peaks and 1.2B tokens/month estimate, do we recommend Hosted with autoscale + smart routing (tier models) or propose Dedicated (reserved capacity)? What pod count for Dedicated to meet 99th pct latency < 400ms for rerank paths?
- Grace: does Titan-40B-32k align with our model verification for hallucination/QA? Any red flags on the 32k plan?
- Marissa/Ben: message for customer — propose canary rollout 10% traffic -> 50% -> 100% over 2 weeks. Confirm acceptance and update Sophie with recommended checkpoints.

+1 on the shortlist, a few infra notes:

- Capacity sizing: for Dedicated with steady 12 RPS and 45 RPS peak, assuming 2x Titan-40B (32k) pods with autoscale buffer to 4 pods for bursts should keep tail latency under 400ms for decode-limited calls if we enable batching for rerank paths. If using Hosted, we should recommend a routing policy that pins rerank to RedGem-13B and routes freeform to Titan to reduce cost.
- Context strategy: because they have occasional larger blobs (purchase history), recommend hybrid approach: 8k as baseline window for most requests, keep Titan-32k variant available for symptomatic calls where the client attaches large context (triggered via per-request header). This way we don't inflate costs for every call.
- Caching: enable prefix/KV caching for templates and rerank inputs; expected token savings ~22% on templates.
- Observability: we should pre-provision sampling for evals and include a regression test suite to flag increases in hallucination for freeform > 1.5x baseline.

I can pull rough perf numbers (p95 latencies) for the three models by EOD and do a cost run for Hosted vs Dedicated.

—Marcus
Infrastructure Lead, Redwood Inference
